requirements.requirement: Create an SSH certificate authority on node1
requirements.summary: Ansible playbook run from node2 generated an ed25519 CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca(.pub) on node1, confirmed present with correct 0600/0700 permissions before and after a reboot.

requirements.requirement: node1's host key is signed by the CA and sshd presents that certificate
requirements.summary: Playbook signed node1's ed25519 host key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with principals node1,10.100.12.10, added HostCertificate/HostKey directives to sshd_config, validated with sshd -t, and restarted sshd. A client SSH session shows the server presenting 'ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com' signed by the CA.
An Ansible inventory and playbook (site.yml) on node2 defines all CA/cert/sshd-config tasks; ansible-playbook run completed ok=14 changed=7 failed=0 against node1.

requirements.requirement: A client that trusts the CA connects to node1 without pinning its host key
requirements.summary: Node2's pinned host-key known_hosts entries for node1/10.100.12.10 were removed; only a @cert-authority trust line with the CA public key was added. A subsequent SSH connection with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes succeeded, with verbose output explicitly showing 'Host is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate' rather than a pinned-key match, and this was reconfirmed after node1's reboot.

overall_summary: The executor built an Ansible playbook run from node2 that created an SSH host CA on node1, signed node1's ed25519 host key into a certificate, configured and validated sshd to present it, and demonstrated end-to-end that a client trusting only the CA (no pinned host key) connects successfully with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes — verbose SSH output confirms certificate-based validation. All four material outcomes of the task contract are directly and coherently satisfied. The mandatory provider-wide node-restart protocol was also completed for both nodes with clear pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities (cross-checked against the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot), and recovered sshd/CA/cert state and CA-trusted connectivity afterward. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found; the one non-task-driven mutation (fixing node1's broken sshd/missing host keys) was a necessary, well-evidenced bootstrap step.
limitations: The baseline image for node1 had sshd already broken (no host keys, start-limit-hit) before any executor action; this diagnostic/remediation step (ssh-keygen -A, enable ssh.service) was outside the literal task wording but was required to make the node reachable at all, and is treated as a legitimate prerequisite rather than an unrequested change.

The lifecycle 'after_prepare' snapshot is an alias of 'before_prepare' (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor differentiation relies solely on the executor timeline and the after_executor snapshot; this is consistent with the disabled prepare phase and not a gap in the evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Every state-changing command traces to either the core task (CA creation, signing, sshd config), a necessary bootstrap prerequisite, or bounded final verification/restart evidence. node1's baseline image had no SSH host keys at all and sshd was in a systemd start-limit-hit failure state (cmd-cac6d76aa8e24cfc discovery); ssh-keygen -A plus enabling ssh.service (cmd-cf5bdff48526473e) was a necessary, low-risk prerequisite to make the node reachable for Ansible/SSH at all, and it was retained since the task requires a working, certificate-authenticated sshd. Provisioning the cluster SSH keypair (cmd-2ec4b19aa92f4a20/cmd-f84bdb620787482e) and writing the Ansible inventory/playbook (cmd-a8d60825bc0b4857, cmd-44101973fe584dc2) are standard, necessary setup and were left in place as intended artifacts, not residue. Removing stale pinned host-key known_hosts entries and adding a @cert-authority line (cmd-c281586ed67a4e90, cmd-d2d091949d6b4d33) is a direct, required action to demonstrate CA-based trust rather than key pinning. Both node reboots were part of the mandated restart-evidence protocol and were fully recovered. No unreverted troubleshooting experiments, conflicting services, or unnecessary broad/destructive mutations were observed; node1's package-health and failed-services checks remain clean after the run.
